title: OpenAI Business Hub shows mentions and clicks, not access
why: Expected a visibility report to explain ChatGPT presence; found mentions and clicks that the tooltip says do not confirm a visit, while the crawl side stays unmeasured.

drafts.text: OpenAI's Business Hub now shows claimed businesses their ChatGPT mentions and website clicks. The tooltip says a click does not confirm a visit. A mention is an outcome a scan cannot measure. Whether crawlers can reach your pages is something a scan can check.

OpenAI's Business Hub went live on 10 November. Claimed businesses can see how often ChatGPT mentions them and how many clicks reach their site. The tooltip adds that a click does not confirm a visit or a conversion, so the number is a starting point, not a result.

I read this as two different things. A mention is an outcome, and a homepage scan cannot predict it. Access is an input. A site can check whether AI crawlers are allowed to read its pages. In our July sample of 219 hand-picked homepages, 14 (6.4%) blocked at least one of ten tracked AI crawlers outright.

Monday morning: open robots.txt and check the ten crawlers before you look at the mention count.

Method note: 219 homepages in six categories, scanned 29 to 31 July 2026, one scan each. The score measures readiness, not presence in answers. Confidence: medium.
